method: Agent-run paired public-prefix rolling-origin replay of actual independently compiled parent and candidate executables. At each t=20..52 both receive only bars 0..t, reset cash=1000 and units=0, fill at t+1 and mark at t+7. Single candidate declared before this replay on reused development data; no parameter sweep. Warmup=21 closes for both. Single declared criterion: higher mean net profit, worst loss and maximum marked drawdown at most 51% of parent, unchanged entry count, and zero candidate rejected fills. Budget is the sole algorithmic change: old 500 dollars, new 250 dollars; no parameter sweep.
limitations: Reused prior-development 60 published index-price bars, 33 overlapping episodes; hypothesis informed by previous metrics and match-2 loss. Halving exposure mechanically reduces both gains and losses; no improved alpha or timing is established. Historical selection bias and reduced upside capture remain. stride-seven subset is a descriptive sensitivity check, not an independent holdout. Hypothesis formulated after scoreboard review; historical selection bias possible. No unseen observations, private judge data or t>59 prices used. Mark-to-market not liquidation; no exit fee charged because competition marks held inventory. Independent matched judge replay is unavailable; this is not judge verification or out-of-sample evidence. Equal 10% fill buffer is not a bound.
fill_policy: Next public close t+1, buy price close*1.0005 plus 0.001 fee on slipped notional. Actual emitted rounded quantity; reject entire entry if cost exceeds cash. No shorting/leverage. Terminal equity cash+units*close[t+7], no forced liquidation; costs and warmup identical. Cases reset; not a cumulative live portfolio.
